**Coleman PowerPack Propane Stove (id: 9003)**:
- 7,500 BTU, single burner
- Has "PerfectFlow pressure-control technology" for steady heat
- Description says "fully adjustable flame lets you boil water or simmer chili"
- BUT: Multiple reviews complain about poor flame control at low settings:
  - "No real control over the burner, setting it to low can be tricky"
  - "The control knob goes from off to full blast in a matter of 1/4 turn"
  - "No easy ability to simmer with this stove. It pretty much runs at a medium or high setting"
  - "the lowest flame is too much for just a simmer"

  - "smooth continuous flame adjustment to be a much welcome improvement"
  - Mixed reviews on flame control

**Stansport Single Burner 10,000 BTU Propane Stove (id: 52235)**:
- 10,000 BTU, single burner
- "The flame has a good control dial and can be turned from a very low flame to a flamin' high flame"
- "the heat control was superior to a number of Coleman propane stoves used over years more reflecting the temperature control of home stoves"
- "I prefer this stove to the Coleman single burner stove, as it allows for a lower cook setting"
- "The thing I love most is the smooth adjustment. You can turn it up high or nice and low for a simmer"

- BUT: Some safety concerns in reviews (gas leaks)
- Available at Walmart under Ozark Trail brand

**GAS ONE B-3000H (id: 119755)**:
- 100,000 BTU - very high output
- Has "integrated heat dial" for flame control
- "heat is controllable & as high or low as you want"
- "Easy to regulate the flame with dial knob"
- "Temperature can be easily control"
- More of a high-power burner, good for brewing, canning, wok cooking

- Some quality concerns (paint issues, safety concerns)

**Coleman Peak 1 (id: 881059)**:
- 10,000 BTU, single burner
- "fully-adjustable heat goes from simmer to full boil"
- "PerfectFlow pressure control technology produces a steady fuel stream"
- "get water boiling then subsequently turn it down to a simmer without any burning"
- Very lightweight (6.7 oz)
- Compact, readily available
- Good for backpacking

**Sportsman SBCIS (id: 355720)**:
- 15,000 BTU, cast iron
- "I'm especially pleased at how sensitive the control is"
- "the temperature adjustment valve...works very well, and seems to have even more precision than my last one"
- BUT: Many quality issues, safety concerns, poor construction

Based on the user's specific need for **precise flame control from simmer to max heat**, the best options appear to be:

1. **Stansport Single Burner 10,000 BTU (id: 52235)** - Multiple reviews specifically praise its smooth flame adjustment and ability to go from very low simmer to high flame. It's widely available (also sold as Ozark Trail at Walmart).

2. **Coleman Peak 1 (id: 881059)** - Described as having "fully-adjustable heat goes from simmer to full boil" with PerfectFlow technology. Very readily available.

3. **GAS ONE B-3000H (id: 119755)** - Has an integrated heat dial for precise control, very high BTU output. Good for those who need maximum heat.

4. **Coleman PowerPack (id: 9003)** - Has PerfectFlow technology and is described as having adjustable flame, though some reviews note the control isn't as smooth as the Stansport.

I think the best recommendations for the user's specific needs (precise flame control, readily available, single burner) are:
- Stansport Single Burner 10,000 BTU (best for precise simmer-to-high control)
- Coleman Peak 1 (best for portability with good flame control)
- GAS ONE B-3000H (best for high heat with adjustable control)
